16 Magazine Covers That Will Trigger the Feminists and SJW's in Your Life

PROBLEM

often when people post media links (image/video/animation), they link to a page that contains all the garbage (ads, widgets, etc.) that i don't want to see - i prefer links that point directly to the media file

typical link example: https://ipfs.pics/QmaMBcVT3idGe67EcMiKgFNxReU9rZ6AXMGV25zH2nff8u

direct link to image: https://ipfs.pics/ipfs/QmaMBcVT3idGe67EcMiKgFNxReU9rZ6AXMGV25zH2nff8u

 

SOLUTION

you'll need a browser extension that can rewrite links automatically and accepts regular expressions - in my case i use Firefox, so i would recommend Redirector, however there are at least several other solutions for Firefox, including Greasemonkey, as well as other browsers (it's up to you to find one)

with your extension installed, you can begin adding patterns to match - here are some examples for Redirector...

 

ipfs.pics

Description: ipfs.pics - direct image link
Example URL: https://ipfs.pics/QmaMBcVT3idGe67EcMiKgFNxReU9rZ6AXMGV25zH2nff8u
Include pattern: https?://ipfs.pics/(.+)
Redirect to: https://ipfs.pics/ipfs/$1
Pattern type: Regular Expression

 

imgur.com

Description: imgur.com - direct image link
Example URL: http://imgur.com/r/gaming/eEXxme5
Include pattern: https?://imgur.com.*/([a-z0-9]+)$
Redirect to: https://imgur.com/$1.jpg
Pattern type: Regular Expression

 

gfycat.com

Description: gfycat.com - direct video link
Example URL: https://gfycat.com/FormalPassionateHagfish
Include pattern: https?://gfycat.com/(.+)
Redirect to: https://fat.gfycat.com/$1.mp4
Pattern type: Regular Expression

 

youtube.com

Description: youtube.com - video embed link
Example URL: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YR83iD01YvM
Include pattern: https?://www.youtube.com/watch?v=(.+)
Redirect to: https://www.youtube.com/embed/$1
Pattern type: Regular Expression

 

READ ME

the above examples may need work - i just started using Redirector and i'm not an expert with RegEx

if you need help, such as to add another site or write an expression, post a comment

you're pretty much spot-on - in the search string (the include pattern) you'll see we're 'capturing' part of the string with the brackets ( )

the full expression is (.+) where the dot will match any single character and the plus means match the previous character, which is any character, 1 or more times - since the file name of the image, video, etc. is an unknown, this is one way to grab and remember it with a regular expression

then in the 'redirect to' string, we're recalling that capture - $1 is for the first capturing group, but if there were more than one then we would use $2, $3, etc.
